answer: A work-backed reputation bridge can resist Sybil attacks: each agent must earn trust by completing verifiable tasks over time, and its standing grows only by a small delta after each success. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand separate work histories, not just one registration, so the attacker pays in compute, time, and fees for every copy. One strong signal of sustained useful work is therefore worth far more than many empty accounts, because fakes cannot shortcut the history real agents accumulate.
